findings.evidence: Two builds from identical committed source produced different totalJavascriptBytes values (818224 and 821521). The build-dependent value was persisted in reports/clinical-platform/accessibility-mobile-performance.json and compared byte-for-byte by currentness.
findings.reproduction: Generate the quality report from two otherwise identical Next.js builds and compare the persisted observed JavaScript byte metrics.
findings.requiredChange: Do not persist invocation-dependent observed bundle metrics as currentness inputs. Keep deterministic limits and enforce them against each current build.
findings.retestResult: pass: a synthetic 3072-byte JavaScript build variance leaves the tracked quality report byte-identical, while the current build remains checked against deterministic 2 MiB total and 256 KiB chunk limits
findings.remainingLimitation: Observed bundle sizes are intentionally ephemeral build evidence. They are enforced during generation and by the performance-budget check, but exact observed bytes are not a reproducible tracked artifact.

findings.evidence: spawnSync captured a full-index binary Git diff using Node's default buffer and failed with ENOBUFS when the patch exceeded 1 MiB.
findings.reproduction: Run repository-state capture with a tracked working-tree patch larger than Node's historical default capture limit.
findings.requiredChange: Set an explicit generous maxBuffer for Git state capture and prove a patch larger than 1 MiB is captured.
findings.retestResult: pass: captured a 2900257-byte synthetic full-index patch with the configured 209715200-byte buffer
findings.remainingLimitation: Capture fails closed if repository changes exceed 200 MiB; this is intentional protection against unbounded child-process output.
